functions.description: Compute the least common multiple of two positive integers
outputs: the least common multiple of the two integers

functions.description: Count the positive multiples of a divisor that do not exceed a limit.
inputs: the divisor whose multiples are counted
the largest value allowed for the counted multiples
outputs: the number of positive multiples of the divisor not exceeding the limit

functions.description: Count positive integers up to a limit that are divisible by at least one divisor in a given list, using inclusion-exclusion over lcms.
inputs: the largest value allowed for the counted integers
the list of divisors of which at least one must divide a counted integer
outputs: the count of positive integers up to the limit divisible by at least one of the divisors

functions.description: Count positive integers below a bound that are divisible by the exclusion divisor and by at least one inclusion divisor, via inclusion-exclusion over lcms.
inputs: the exclusive upper bound N for the positive integers being counted, as a positive integer
the set of inclusion divisors d1 or d2 (positive integers) such that a counted integer must be divisible by at least one of them
the exclusion divisor d (a positive integer) such that counted integers must not be divisible by it
outputs: the count of positive integers less than N divisible by the exclusion divisor and by at least one inclusion divisor

functions.description: Count positive integers below a bound that are divisible by some inclusion divisor but not by the exclusion divisor.
inputs: the exclusive upper bound N for the positive integers being counted, as a positive integer
the set of inclusion divisors d1 or d2 (positive integers) such that a counted integer must be divisible by at least one of them
the exclusion divisor d (a positive integer) such that counted integers must not be divisible by it
outputs: the count of positive integers less than N divisible by an inclusion divisor but not by the exclusion divisor

entry_points.text: How many positive integers less than ●1 are divisible by ●2 but not by ●3?

params.description: the exclusive upper bound N for the positive integers being counted, as a positive integer
params.validity_range: N must be a positive integer. Any N >= 2 is valid and gives a well-defined count over {1, ..., N-1}. N = 1 is degenerate and yields 0. Non-integer or non-positive bounds are not meaningful for this counting problem. Very large N is valid but only affects computation cost, not logic.

params.description: the set of inclusion divisors d1 or d2 (positive integers) such that a counted integer must be divisible by at least one of them
params.validity_range: Each divisor must be a positive integer, at least 2 to be non-trivial. A divisor of 1 would make every integer qualify, which is logically valid but trivial. Divisors may be any positive integers, including ones sharing factors (e.g. 4 and 6); inclusion-exclusion over lcms handles overlap. The list should be non-empty for a meaningful count.

params.description: the exclusion divisor d (a positive integer) such that counted integers must not be divisible by it
params.validity_range: The exclusion divisor must be a positive integer. A value of 1 would exclude every integer and make the count 0, which is logically valid but degenerate. Any integer >= 2 is valid. The exclusion divisor may share factors with the inclusion divisors; the subtraction step handles the overlap correctly.

entry_points.text: How many positive integers less than 1000 are divisible by 3 or 5 but not by 7?
